title: Priority Colouring
body:
An undirected graph has n vertices numbered 1 to n. There are 10 colours, numbered 1 (highest priority) to 10 (lowest).

Colour the vertices in order 1, 2, …, n. Each vertex gets the highest-priority colour (the smallest number) that is not already used by one of its already coloured neighbours.

Print the colour of every vertex.

Function to complete

Complete colourVertices(n, edges). It returns the colour of vertices 1 to n.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: The first line contains n and m. Each of the next m lines contains an edge u v.
out: n integers separated by spaces: the colour of vertices 1 to n.
cons: Every vertex has at most 9 neighbours, so 10 colours always suffice

samples.ex: A path alternates between colours 1 and 2.
Vertex 3 touches 1 (colour 1) and 2 (colour 2), so it gets 3. Vertex 4 touches 1 and 3, so it gets 2.

if __name__ == "__main__":
    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    n = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _m = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    edges = [list(map(int, _t[_p + _i * 2:_p + (_i + 1) * 2])) for _i in range((_m))]; _p += (_m) * 2
    _r = Solution().colourVertices(n, edges)
    print(" ".join(map(str, _r)))
